blocks.text: An AI assistant for Outlook on Mac answers questions about the window you have open, points at the control you need, and types text where your cursor sits. Lazur does those things. Hold ⌥⌘, ask in plain words, and Lazur answers out loud while it looks at your screen. It does not click for you, and it is not an add-in for Outlook.
What an AI assistant for Outlook on Mac actually does

Outlook for Mac is a window full of small controls. Most people use a handful of them every day and guess at the rest. An assistant on your Mac helps with the guessing. It is a helper, not a pilot. You still choose, click and send.

items: Explains what is on screen, such as a notice, an error or a setting you do not recognize.
Points at a control with a circle and a label, so you know where to click.
Guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it gives the next step.
Drafts text and types it at the cursor when you ask.
Dictates clean text at the cursor while you hold fn.

blocks.text: Lazur does not click buttons, send messages, move mail or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and Lazur has no partnerships with any app maker. If you want a message sent, you press Send. Keep that rule in mind from the first minute, because it shapes every ask that follows.
Check your Outlook version before you ask for help

Microsoft ships two Outlook clients on Mac. The new Outlook for Mac is the current one. Microsoft's end-of-support page says that starting October 2026, legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes. That date has already passed. Microsoft also says Exchange Web Services is fully disabled in April 2027.

Open the Outlook menu and choose About Outlook to read your build number. The current build in Microsoft's release notes is 16.114.3 (build 26102720), released October 27, 2026. Microsoft's features page describes the new Outlook for Mac as version 16.58 and later.

The switch from legacy is where people get stuck. One Microsoft Q&A thread from June 16, 2026 asks why the poster was moved off legacy. The same thread reports that search does not work, rules no longer work and junk reporting fails. An AI-generated answer on that thread says Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook exists for 16.58 and later. Treat that answer as unverified, because it is not a Microsoft staff statement. Some products no longer have the toggle, so check your Help menu before you rely on it.

blocks.text: Explain what is on screen when Outlook confuses you

The most common question is a plain one: what is this? A bar at the top of a message, a grey strip, a setting you did not change. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask. Lazur looks at the screen, explains the thing in plain words and answers out loud. It looks only while you hold the keys, so ask at the moment you see the problem.

Explanations depend on what is visible. If a notice is cut off, expand it or scroll to the text first, then ask again. Quote the exact words when you can. “What does retention mean in this box” works better than “what is this thing.” Lazur can explain a term. It cannot tell you what your admin configured unless that setting is shown on your screen.
Point at a button you cannot find

Buttons move between builds, and some commands are faster by key than by eye. Microsoft's keyboard table lists ⇧⌘M for moving the selected item. If you cannot find Move on your build, ask: “Where is the Move button?” Lazur draws a circle and a label around the control on your screen. You click it. Lazur does not press it.

Bring Outlook to the front before you hold the keys. Lazur answers about the screen you have, so a Finder window in front gives you a Finder answer. Point the question at the window you mean. That one habit avoids most of the confusion people report with on-screen help.
Walk through a feature one click at a time

Some tasks take five steps and a menu you never open. Ask Lazur to guide you, and it gives one step, then waits for your click before it gives the next. That pacing matters in a mail client. A wrong click can file a message in the wrong folder, and you may not notice until later.

Here is a worked example. Ask: “Walk me through putting the reading pane on the right.” If you already know the shortcut, ask for that instead. Microsoft lists ⌘\ for the reading pane on the right and ⇧⌘\ for below. A walkthrough is slower than a shortcut when you know the key. Use the walkthrough for menus you have not learned yet.
Draft text at the cursor

A blank reply takes longer than it should. Click into the message body, so the cursor blinks where you want the text. Then ask for a draft. Lazur types the text at the cursor, so you edit in place rather than copy and paste.

Give it the facts. Say: “Draft a reply saying I need two more days and will send the file Friday.” Name the date, the number and the tone. Lazur does not know your deadline unless you say it. Read the draft before you send. Check every name, date and figure, because an unread draft is an easy way to send a wrong date.
Dictate a reply with fn

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is included on both paid plans and is unlimited there, so you can talk through a long reply. Speak in full sentences. Short pauses help the text break where you expect it to.

Use the personal dictionary for names and product words that dictation gets wrong. Snippets cover sign-offs you type every day. Clipboard slots hold a link or a figure while you dictate around it. Check the cursor first. Dictation lands in whatever field has focus, so a cursor in the To line puts your sentence in the address box.
Where Outlook for Mac slows people down

Microsoft does not publish a ranked list of Outlook help topics, so this is a qualitative read, not a count. Three complaints show up in Microsoft's own pages and Q&A threads: search, rules and junk handling in the new client. The June 16, 2026 thread describes search that does not work, rules that no longer work, and junk reporting that fails, so junk returns to the inbox.

Microsoft's features page also lists five items as under investigation for the new client. Those include Search across all items, Show folder size and Address Book / Browsable GAL. It lists 12 features as not available in the new client, including Compose in plaintext, Status bar and Search Feedback. Those gaps matter only if you rely on them, so list the features you use before you switch.

Lazur cannot repair search or rules. It can explain what the screen shows when a search returns nothing, and it can point at the filter or rules pane while you check. Treat it as a reader of your screen, not a repair tool.
How much mail a Mac user handles each day

Microsoft WorkLab reports that the average worker receives 117 emails daily. The same report says employees are interrupted every 2 minutes during core work hours by meetings, email or notifications. Those figures come from Microsoft 365 telemetry ending February 15, 2025, so read them as a snapshot, not a forecast.

The 400 million figure is older and easy to misread. Microsoft's FY24 Q2 release, quoted in a January 2024 post, says Office 365 had over 400 million paid seats. A seat is a paid license, not a person who opens Outlook each day. Do not use it as a count of Outlook users.
Those numbers explain why short help matters. A question you can ask out loud beats reading a help article from top to bottom while your next meeting starts.
macOS versions and the requirements conflict

Microsoft's pages disagree on the minimum macOS. The release notes say macOS 14 (Sonoma) is the minimum to receive updates to Microsoft 365 and Office apps. They also say macOS 12 (Monterey) is the minimum to install versions 16.78 or later. The Outlook for Mac support page still says macOS 10.14 (Mojave) or later. Treat the release notes as the newer source.

An older macOS may still run Outlook, but it gets no more updates, including security updates. Check the App Store listing for Outlook before you install. Check your own version under the Apple menu > About This Mac. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs, so the chip is not the limit.
Asking well: window, goal and exact words

Good asks have three parts. Name the window, state the goal and quote the words on screen. Compare “why is this broken” with “I am replying to this message and the Send button looks grey. What does that mean?” The second gives Lazur a window, a goal and a clue.

Edge case: if you have two Outlook windows open, close the one you do not mean. Lazur reads what is visible, so a stray window can change the answer. If an answer seems off, ask again after you bring the right window forward.
Privacy: what gets sent when you hold the key

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Your content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did stays on your Mac.

Practical rule: if a window shows mail you should not share, close it before you hold the keys. Lazur sees what is on screen, and the screenshot goes out to answer. That habit costs nothing and works for any AI tool.
Pricing and a free trial

Lazur has a free trial that needs no credit card. There are two paid plans, Pro and Power, and dictation is unlimited on both. The plans differ in how many AI actions they include. Compare current prices on the [pricing page](/pricing) before you choose, because prices can change.
Mistakes to avoid in your first week

items: Holding ⌥⌘ while Outlook sits behind another window, then trusting the answer.
Sending a draft you did not read, including names, dates and figures.
Dictating with the cursor in the To or Subject line.
Skipping the macOS check and finding out about an update wall later.
Using Lazur to test search or rules, then blaming Lazur when Outlook fails. Test those in Outlook itself.
Forgetting that some macOS settings and utilities can override Outlook shortcuts. Check System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts when a key does nothing.

blocks.text: A practical first hour

Start with three asks: what is on screen, where is a button, and draft one short reply. Each one tests a different part of the tool. Then check your Outlook build, your macOS version and your search. If search fails, you learn that in the first hour, not on the day a deadline lands.

faq.question: Is Lazur an add-in for Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It runs on your Mac, looks at the screen only while you hold ⌥⌘, and answers out loud. It works alongside Outlook, and Lazur has no partnerships with any app maker.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with the new Outlook for Mac and legacy Outlook?
faq.answer: Lazur reads what is on your screen, so the window you show it matters more than the client name. Microsoft calls the new Outlook for Mac the current client. Legacy Outlook stopped working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. Check your build with Outlook > About Outlook first.

faq.question: Will Lazur send my email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It can type a draft at the cursor, but you review it and press Send yourself.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Outlook for Mac need?
faq.answer: Microsoft's release notes say macOS 14 (Sonoma) is the minimum to receive Office updates, and macOS 12 (Monterey) to install version 16.78 or later. The Outlook for Mac support page still lists macOS 10.14 (Mojave) or later. Check the App Store listing before you install.

faq.question: Does Lazur listen all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Does dictation work inside Outlook?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Microsoft lists its own Advanced dictation only for the new Outlook for Mac, so treat Lazur's dictation and Microsoft's feature as separate tools.

faq.question: Is Lazur available on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, not available. This page covers the Mac app only.
